title: Codex tool wrappers (howto)
desc: How the Claude-named cmd wrappers route Codex tool calls through the harness, and the calling conventions.
steps: ARCHITECTURE: Codex native write_file/read_file are blocked (config.toml hook exit 2); Codex must shell out to cmd wrappers named after Claude built-ins -- Edit.cmd Write.cmd Read.cmd Glob.cmd Grep.cmd. Each reads stdin JSON matching the Claude tool_input shape (Edit: {tool_name:Edit,tool_input:{file_path,old_string,new_string}}) and pipes it UNCHANGED to wkharness.ps1, so every existing guard fires identically -- zero harness changes.
INSTALL: wkwrap --install mklinks WKAppBot/bin/Edit.cmd -> personal-docs/tools/Edit.cmd (symlinks, no wk prefix).
CLI-ARG FALLBACK: all shims detect [Console]::IsInputRedirected; when false (Codex subprocess, empty stdin) positional args are promoted to JSON (args-first inversion avoids the ReadToEnd hang).

MULTILINE CONVENTION: from BASH/Claude-Code use a single-quoted heredoc (Agent.cmd --model X << QUOTE-EOF ... EOF); from CODEX/PowerShell use a PS here-string (@' ... '@ at column 0) -- a bash heredoc fails inside PowerShell. Single-line ASCII may be a quoted arg.

MODEL ALIASES stay DISTINCT: codex / gpt-mini / codex-mini / gpt are DIFFERENT models, not synonyms -- verify modelUsage after a cross-family dispatch (codex may silently fall back to haiku when the CLI is absent).
